summary: Checked before any route, on every request whatever its method and path - the dashboard at / and a path no route has included - in this order, the first that refuses answering. Its routes are asked by programs - an application's server, a holder - and never from a browser; its one page is the dashboard, the operator's, served from its own address. THE NAME IT WAS SENT TO (its Host): a request whose Host is not one of the coordinator's own names - 127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], the address it listens on, and the host of each page it was started to allow - is refused 403 host_not_allowed. A website whose name is made to point at this machine (DNS rebinding) sends that name as its Host and as its Origin, and would otherwise pass for the dashboard: it is refused whatever it asks, and so is a request with no Origin that names a host the coordinator does not have. A name is compared in lower case and without its port; a Host that is not a name and a port is refused. A request that names no Host at all is answered as before: every browser names one. THE PAGE THAT SENT IT (its Origin): a request that carries an Origin header is refused 403 origin_not_allowed unless its Origin is the coordinator's own - the address the request was sent to: http:// and its Host, which is the dashboard - or a page's address the coordinator was started to allow (--allow-origin, written as a browser writes a page's address: scheme, host and port; none by default). So a web page from anywhere else can never ask for the card, give a port back or read the record, not even with a request a browser sends without asking first (a form's POST, or a text body). ITS BODY, whatever the method: a request that names a Transfer-Encoding - a body sent in chunks, its length never said - is refused 411 length_required, whether or not it names a Content-Length too: the coordinator reads a body by its Content-Length alone; a request whose Content-Length is more than the coordinator reads (--max-body, 1 MiB by default) is refused 413 too_large before a byte of its body is read; a Content-Length that is not a whole number of bytes reads as no body. A body within the cap that no route reads - a refused request's, a GET's - is read and set aside before the answer; a body the coordinator does not read - in chunks, or over the cap - is never read at all: its answer says Connection: close, and the connection is closed a moment after the answer is out - so an asker still sending hears the answer, not a reset. ITS TIME: a request must arrive whole - its first line, its headers and its body - within --read-timeout seconds (10 by default) of its connection being made. One that has not is never answered: its connection is closed, and a request cut off part way is said on the coordinator's console. Only a page the coordinator was started to allow is ever told it may read an answer: Access-Control-Allow-Origin naming it, and Vary: Origin, on every answer it is given - a refusal before any route included. A refusal for any other page carries no Access-Control header: the browser shows the page nothing. A request with no Origin, sent to one of the coordinator's own names, and one from the dashboard, are answered exactly as if there were no check. An allowed page's preflight - OPTIONS, from that page - is answered 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type. A method no route takes - HEAD, PUT, DELETE, any other - is checked the same way, and then answered 501, as http.server answers a method it does not take; so is OPTIONS with no Origin, or from the dashboard. A refusal before any route is said on the coordinator's console, and never written to its record: a page must not be able to fill the record by asking.
